reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage account creation with an invitation to earn, participant claims of millions of rupees in income and substantial team growth, and an approximately stated payment for the possibility of million-rupee earnings. The speaker's assurance that the platform is not fraudulent is promotional countercontext, while the accuracy of the figures and exact payment flow are not established.

I have made a team of 200,000 in a short period of one year and seven months.
the person who gave you the link to this meeting, go and contact him and make your account.
After that, even those who are coming with your reference will be incorporated.
make almost round about of 3,900 rupees to make an account of that money and earn million rupees

opening.argument: Judge the presentation by what it invites the audience to examine, not by treating its assurance of safety as proof of safety. The speaker asks listeners to identify weak points and raise them for discussion, then makes the system's security a stated topic. That does not amount to a formal risk warning, but it gives the audience an explicit opening to question the claims. On this record, the stronger reading is a discussion and examination of a platform, without independently accepting its assurances.

citations.quote: If you notice any weak point anywhere, you have to hold that and tell me in the end
how secure and strong is this system?

rebuttal.rebuttal: The account invitation in the opening statement is real, but it does not erase the speaker's invitation to challenge weak points. Nor does the stated account cost establish what happens to that money or whether earnings are guaranteed. Those gaps matter before treating the presentation's claims as an established deceptive scheme.

citations.quote: If you notice any weak point anywhere, you have to hold that and tell me in the end
make almost round about of 3,900 rupees to make an account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An invitation to point out weak spots is not a risk disclosure. The same presentation tells viewers to make an account and start earning, while presenting the initial account cost as a route to million-rupee earnings. A chance to ask questions does not change the function of those solicitations.

citations.quote: go and get your account made and start earning from here.
make almost round about of 3,900 rupees to make an account of that money and earn million rupees

opening.argument: The judge should give substantial weight to what the speaker actually does: invite viewers to follow a process on their own phones, look up what Forsage is, and discuss creating a wallet. The sampled screens also show an account-preview input and a page headed with that same explanatory question. These are concrete features of an operational demonstration. Testimonials may be part of the meeting, but they need not define the entire video as a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: I am working on the process in front of you and you can also do the same in your mobile.
We will open Google again and write what is Forsage?
To create its wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening statement correctly quotes invitations to join, but those invitations occur alongside a walkthrough viewers can follow on a phone. A participant's claimed team size does not, by itself, explain how anyone is paid. The cited references show a social route into the meeting, not the terms of a commission plan.

citations.quote: you can also do the same in your mobile.
I have made a team of 200,000 in a short period of one year and seven months.
the person who gave you the link to this meeting, go and contact him and make your account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is part of the recruitment pitch: after discussing account creation, the speaker links the account cost to earning millions. A participant then directs viewers back to the person who supplied their meeting link to make an account. Showing the steps does not make the solicitation merely educational.

citations.quote: make almost round about of 3,900 rupees to make an account of that money and earn million rupees
the person who gave you the link to this meeting, go and contact him and make your account.

opening.argument: A referral-linked business presentation is not enough, on its own, to establish a recruitment-payment mechanism. The video calls itself a network-marketing blockchain project, discusses making an account, and says newcomers who arrive through a viewer's reference will be incorporated. But those statements do not specify a commission, a tier, or a payment triggered by recruiting someone. The cited earnings are personal claims, not an explanation of their source. Judge the observed offer as business promotion without inferring payout rules the presentation does not show.

citations.quote: Network marketing blockchain technology
make almost round about of 3,900 rupees to make an account
even those who are coming with your reference will be incorporated.
I have earned 3.2 million rupees from this forex.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening combines team growth, a meeting-link referral, and account cost. That combination warrants scrutiny, but none of its quotations says an existing participant receives a commission when the next person pays. Even the speaker's account of a large team leaves the relationship between team size and earnings unstated. The precise recruitment-payment mechanism remains an inference.

citations.quote: I have made a team of 200,000 in a short period of one year and seven months.
the person who gave you the link to this meeting, go and contact him and make your account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The case does not depend on proving an exact commission schedule. The presentation pairs extraordinary income claims and team growth with instructions to return to the meeting-link provider and make an account; it also says people arriving through a participant's reference will be incorporated. Those connections support a recruitment-centered earning pitch, even though the payout rules remain unshown.
